builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Raincheck: Deferred Multimodal Prefill for Efficient Multi-Turn MLLM Inference
summary: Replaces one-shot full multimodal prefill (and irreversible query-aware hard pruning) with an initial pruned prefill whose dropped tokens are progressively prefilled during decode and post-answer scheduling gaps, using attention visibility control and affine state mapping to update context mid-conversation. Costs: retention of unselected tokens and their state on the serving path, added scheduler and attention-mask complexity, integration against a specific engine (SGLang) and models (Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen3.5-9B), and a small TPOT increase. Can fail when later turns need still-unprefilled tokens, when decode gaps are absent under high load so deferred prefill never completes, and because the quality and latency results are validated only on two benchmarks and two models.
rationale: It is a serving-side scheduling technique that fits a single-GPU self-hosted stack and requires no retraining, but the TTFT and quality gains are benchmark- and implementation-specific, so the reader should validate it against their own multi-turn multimodal workload before adopting it in production.
technique: Deferred multimodal prefill with background token backfill

claims.statement: Replaces one-shot full multimodal prefill (and irreversible query-aware hard pruning) with an initial pruned prefill whose dropped tokens are progressively prefilled during decode and post-answer scheduling gaps, using attention visibility control and affine state mapping to update context mid-conversation. Costs: retention of unselected tokens and their state on the serving path, added scheduler and attention-mask complexity, integration against a specific engine (SGLang) and models (Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen3.5-9B), and a small TPOT increase. Can fail when later turns need still-unprefilled tokens, when decode gaps are absent under high load so deferred prefill never completes, and because the quality and latency results are validated only on two benchmarks and two models.

Reduces mean first-turn TTFT by up to 24.1% relative to full prefill on MultiVerse, with less than 0.5% increase in mean TPOT; recovers on average 77.7% and 60.4% of the quality lost to matched hard pruning on MultiVerse and ConvBench with 30% initial multimodal-token retention.
